summary: Two independent backends exist. (1) terminal.rs = PTY layer. TerminalManager (Tauri managed state) holds sessions: Arc<Mutex<HashMap<u64, Arc<TerminalSession>>>> plus AtomicU64 next_id. start_terminal(id?, account_id, cols, rows, command?, project_dir?) -> u64: loads settings, resolves the account (its codex_home dir is created; if account.bypass, ensure_codex_bypass_config writes approvals/sandbox bypass into <CODEX_HOME>/config.toml), resolves cwd (UI workspace param wins over account.project_dir), opens a portable_pty NativePtySystem pty (min 8 rows/20 cols). Crucially it does NOT spawn codex directly: it spawns the user shell from settings.shell (default powershell.exe on Windows with -NoLogo; $SHELL else /bin/sh on Unix) with env CODEX_HOME, TERM=xterm-256color, COLORTERM=truecolor, PWD, optional HTTP(S)_PROXY/ALL_PROXY (6 variants), and CST_ROOM_TOKEN when the agent-room MCP is enabled (room.provision_home merges an MCP entry pointing at http://127.0.0.1:<agent_room.port>/mcp into the account config, then registers AgentMeta{agent_id:"codex", account_id, label, cwd}). The Codex CLI is then launched by WRITING a command line + "\r" into the pty (command param, else account.startup_command). The frontend builds that line: agent.command (default "codex") + "--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox" (per-account bypass, default true), and "codex [flag] resume <uuid>" for resumes. A reader thread pumps 8KB chunks, lossy-UTF8 decodes, and emits Tauri event "pty-data" {id:u64, data:string}; on EOF it records metrics, deregisters the room token, and emits "pty-exit" {id}. A synthetic French banner is also emitted as fake pty-data. write_terminal(id,data) writes+flushes; resize_terminal(id,cols,rows); stop_terminal(id) removes+kills child. There is ZERO output parsing/scraping in Rust — raw ANSI bytes go straight to xterm.js; session-uuid capture happens frontend-side via claim_session_for_terminal polling (rollout files in CODEX_HOME). (2) pool.rs = NOT a pty pool. It is an OpenAI-compatible HTTP facade (axum router: POST /v1/chat/completions, GET /v1/models, GET /admin/status) over the same accounts' CODEX_HOME/auth.json OAuth tokens: round-robin acquire with per-account status (Idle/Busy/Refreshing/Cooling/Banned/Missing), auto token refresh against auth.openai.com (persisted back to auth.json atomically), per-account proxy reqwest clients, forwards to {upstream}/backend-api/codex/responses with chatgpt-account-id/OpenAI-Beta:responses=experimental/originator:codex_cli_rs headers, and re-shapes Codex Responses SSE (response.output_text.delta / response.completed / errors) into chat.completion.chunk SSE. Tools are stripped ("tools":[], store:false), so the pool gives plain streaming text only.
keyFacts: Codex CLI is never spawned as the pty process: the pty runs a shell (settings.shell, default powershell.exe -NoLogo on Windows) and the codex command line is typed into it via writer.write_all(command + "\r") in start_terminal (terminal.rs lines 260-268)

Effective codex launch line is built in src/main.ts agentRunCommand(): `codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` (bypass per-account, default true); resume = `codex [bypass] resume <uuid>` (buildResumeCommand line 661)

Env for the pty: CODEX_HOME=<expanded account.codex_home>, TERM=xterm-256color, COLORTERM=truecolor, PWD=<cwd>, HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY (+lowercase) if account proxy enabled, CST_ROOM_TOKEN=<unique token> if agent_room enabled; cwd = UI workspace param > account.project_dir > none

Frontend receives ONLY raw ANSI bytes via Tauri event "pty-data" {id:u64, data:string} and a terminal-death signal "pty-exit" {id:u64}; there is no structured/message-level parsing of the codex stream anywhere in Rust

A synthetic banner line ("[Codex Switch Terminal] session #N | compte: ... | CODEX_HOME: ... | projet: ... | proxy: ...") is emitted as fake pty-data right after spawn — a chat UI must filter or replace it

pool.rs is a multi-ACCOUNT HTTP rotation pool (not pre-warmed pty sessions): it exposes local OpenAI-compatible POST /v1/chat/completions backed by each account's CODEX_HOME/auth.json access_token, with round-robin, 401/403->Banned, 429->Cooling(cooldown_secs_429), refresh via https://auth.openai.com/oauth/token (client_id fallback app_EMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann), tokens re-persisted to auth.json

Pool upstream call: POST {upstream}/backend-api/codex/responses, headers Authorization Bearer, chatgpt-account-id, OpenAI-Beta: responses=experimental, originator: codex_cli_rs, session_id: sess-<ts>, UA codex_cli_rs/0.45.0; SSE parsing keys on response.output_text.delta / response.completed / response.failed / error / response.incomplete

Pool request body hardcodes "tools": [], "parallel_tool_calls": false, "store": false — so the existing /v1/chat/completions endpoint can power a plain chat UI but CANNOT produce tool-call cards or agentic file edits

Codex session UUID association is frontend-driven: captureCodexSessionId polls invoke("claim_session_for_terminal", {accountId, afterUnix, excludeSessionIds, matchSessionId}) with backoff delays [1200..10000]ms after launch — implying rollout files under CODEX_HOME are scanned server-side and are an available source of structured transcript data
PTY ids: frontend pre-reserves ids (ptyIdSeed) and passes id to start_terminal; backend falls back to its own AtomicU64 when id is None; sizes clamped to min 8 rows / 20 cols on both spawn and resize
Terminal lifecycle metrics: TerminalSession stores started_at/account_id/account_label; finish_session records an agent run exactly once (recorded_end AtomicBool) on kill or natural EOF
launch_ide(command, project_dir?) spawns a detached editor process (cmd.exe /S /C + CREATE_NO_WINDOW on Windows) — separate from pty flow
All user-facing error strings are French (e.g. "Compte Codex introuvable", "Session terminal introuvable")

Local OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint from pool.rs: POST http://localhost:{pool.port}/v1/chat/completions (SSE chat.completion.chunk stream), GET /v1/models, GET /admin/status (account health JSON) — a ready-made structured streaming backend for a pure chat mode, minus tool calls

Agent-room MCP server http://127.0.0.1:{agent_room.port}/mcp with per-terminal CST_ROOM_TOKEN env — existing structured side-channel between running Codex agents and the app (RoomState.register/deregister in terminal.rs lines 165-190, 246-249)

claim_session_for_terminal Tauri command + Codex rollout JSONL files under CODEX_HOME — path to structured message history without ANSI scraping (used today only to grab the session uuid for `codex resume`)

Frontend session model in src/main.ts: TerminalSession objects with ptyId/accountId/codexSessionId, listeners for pty-data/pty-exit, persistTerminalSessions — the state layer a chat view would sit beside or replace
risks: No structured agent protocol today: the only live Codex output is raw ANSI TUI bytes over pty-data; scraping that into chat bubbles/tool cards is extremely fragile (Codex redraws its TUI with cursor moves). A chat UI should switch launch mode to `codex exec --json` / `codex proto` / app-server, or tail rollout JSONL — which changes how start_terminal builds/injects the command

The pool's /v1/chat/completions path forces "tools": [] and store:false, so reusing it for the chat UI gives text-only completions with no tool-call events and no persistent Codex session — it cannot render OpenCode-style tool cards as-is

Startup command is typed into a live shell prompt (write of `cmd\r` right after spawn) with no readiness check; shell banners/prompts and the synthetic app banner will pollute any transcript parser, and a slow shell start could swallow the command

Session-id capture is heuristic (time-window polling of rollout files, exclusion lists, retry backoff) — pairing a chat transcript to the correct Codex session inherits this raciness, especially with multiple simultaneous terminals on one account

Desktop vs web divergence: frontend passes repoUrl/workspacePath/branch/agentId to start_terminal which the desktop terminal.rs signature ignores; server.rs (web mode) has a different variant — any chat redesign must handle both platforms (src/platform.ts)

Bypass flag --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox is on by default per account and also baked into config.toml; a chat UI adding approval-style tool cards would conflict with this always-approve setup unless bypass is made mode-dependent

PTY kill path (stop_terminal) kills the shell child; the codex process is a grandchild typed into the shell — kill semantics may leave codex running on some platforms if the shell doesn't propagate signals
